name: Zhao Jiande
summary:
Zhao Jiande was the last king of Nanyue, ruling from 112 BC until his execution by Western Han forces in 110 BCE. He played a crucial role in the politics of ancient China during the Han dynasty.

Zhao Jiande's reign was marked by power struggles with other regional powers and his efforts to maintain control over his kingdom. Despite these challenges, he managed to preserve Nanyue's independence for several years.

The fall of Nanyue had significant consequences for the region, leading to a power vacuum that was eventually filled by the Han dynasty. This event marked the beginning of a new era in Chinese history and paved the way for the consolidation of imperial power in China.

Zhao Jiande's legacy is still remembered today as a symbol of resistance against foreign occupation and a testament to the enduring spirit of Chinese nationalism.

He was the son of Zhao Qianzhi, who had unified Nanyue under his rule. Despite his efforts, Zhao Jiande was unable to overcome the military might of the Han dynasty and was eventually executed in 110 BCE.
